stemMd: Researchers compare a new treatment with usual care by randomly assigning eligible volunteers to groups. What is the main inferential advantage of random assignment?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It ensures the sample perfectly represents every population.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It guarantees that every patient improves.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It reduces systematic baseline differences between treatment groups.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It makes a control group unnecessary.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It removes all measurement error automatically.

explanationMd: Random allocation helps balance known and unknown baseline factors in expectation. This supports causal comparison, but does not guarantee outcomes, population representativeness or error-free measurement.

distractorRationale.d: The comparison still requires a control.
distractorRationale.e: Measurement quality remains a separate issue.
distractorRationale.a: Random assignment is not the same as random sampling.
